Thanks Mateo — quick read through and comments below.

Short answer: 120 GPU-weeks/month is right on the cusp of requiring a Dedicated pool for predictable latency SLAs. If Octavian's sustained qps is fairly even, we can satisfy with a Dedicated reserve sized to cover the 95th percentile, plus a 30% burst allowance. If they are spiky (onboarding models or evaluation runs), we should recommend a Dedicated baseline of ~90 GPU-weeks/month + a burst plan for the remaining.

Notes: 
- Mapping: 1 "GPU-week" in our sizing doc = ~168 GPU-hours at typical batch rates; easy to convert to pool slots.
- Lead time: procurement and zone provisioning for a Dedicated pool with this capacity is ~6–8 weeks in our current cloud regions, maybe longer if they need a private deployment.
- Impact: reserve sizing today will lock monthly commit and pricing; any changes after booking incur a requote.

I updated the sizing tab in Octavian_MAAP_Sizing.xlsx with a baseline vs burst split and highlighted the 95th percentile column.

Onboarding question for Rebecca (copied): what percentage of their runs are expected to be long-sequence / memory-heavy? That affects whether we recommend higher-memory GPUs or more slots.

Laura Bennett
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

Quick finance view and a pragmatic ask from FinOps: 

- 12-month commit vs Q-by-Q: 12-month gives ~18% lower unit price in our latest pricing model; however, it increases risk exposure if Octavian's usage doesn't ramp.
- Recommendation: propose a stepped commit — 6-month firm with a 6-month optional extension at fixed pricing. That lets us reduce price while keeping runway flexibility.
- For this week: I need a clear mapping from deal GROSS ARR to committed GPU-weeks per month so I can build the reserved revenue schedule into our forecast. Please drop the mapping (ARR -> GPU-weeks -> monthly $) into the "Deal economics" tab of the Drive doc.

Also flagged: if they require private deployment (on-prem/VPC), add ~2–3 weeks to lead time for KMS/HSM and network validation.
